title: Production Reliability and Availability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Production Reliability and Availability”?
options: Assume resource limits improve every workload automatically.
Use a host CPU percentage as a universal performance measurement without context.
Measure a repeatable baseline and change one limit or variable at a time.
questions.answer_key: Measure a repeatable baseline and change one limit or variable at a time.
questions.explanation: Resource tuning is workload- and platform-dependent; compare measured behavior instead of assuming a setting is beneficial.

questions.prompt: For a lab covering production reliability and availability, what is the strongest evidence of learning?
options: Make several unrelated changes before collecting a baseline.
Use a production host so the result looks realistic.
Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
Assume the command is portable and skip reading its output.
questions.answer_key: Record the command or configuration, predicted result, observed evidence, and one relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: A useful lab connects a predicted result to actual output and checks an edge case. This is safer and more reproducible than assuming success.

questions.prompt: If an example related to production reliability and availability fails, which response is best?
options: Trust the image tag without inspecting the image or version.
Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
Delete every stopped container and unused volume before investigating.
Disable permissions or security controls until the example works.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect state/logs/configuration, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The evidence-led approach keeps the diagnosis reproducible and avoids hiding the cause. For production reliability and availability, verify the fix with the exact setting or command that failed.
